Mañon''' (born December 9, 2001) is a Dominican-American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Coachella Valley Lakers]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Cornell Big Red men's basketball|Cornell Big Red]] and [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt Commodores]]. ==Early life and high school career== Mañon was born on December 9, 2001, in [[New Milford, New Jersey]], and is of Dominican descent.{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Chris-Manon/USA/Cornell-University/430247|website=[[Eurobasket.com]]|title=Chris Manon|access-date=July 25, 2025}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/warriors/article/warriors-beat-grizzlies-buoyed-undrafted-wing-20768522.php|newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|via=[[archive.today]]|title=Warriors get past Grizzlies, buoyed by undrafted wing Chris Manon's steady two-way play|date=July 15, 2025|author=Gordon, Sam|archive-url=https://archive.today/20250725173811/https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/warriors/article/warriors-beat-grizzlies-buoyed-undrafted-wing-20768522.php|archive-date=2025-07-25}} He attended [[Saint Joseph Regional High School]] in [[Montvale, New Jersey|Montvale]], where he was named first-team all-league, all-county and all-region as a [[Senior (education)|senior]], when he averaged 12.4 points per game.{{Cite web|url=https://cornellbigred.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/chris-manon/75062|publisher=[[Cornell Big Red]]|title=Chris Manon|access-date=July 25, 2025}} He transferred to [[St. Thomas More School (Connecticut)|St. Thomas School]] for the 2019–20 season, where he was selected second-team All-[[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council]] (NEPSAC).{{Cite web|url=https://www.usbasket.com/NCAA1/news/867529/Former-players:-Chris-Manon-commits-to-Vanderbilt|website=USBasket.com|title=Chris Manon commits to Vanderbilt|date=April 24, 2024}} After high school, he committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Cornell Big Red men's basketball|Cornell]]. ==College career== Mañon played three seasons at Cornell, missing the 2020–21 season, his [[freshman]] year, which was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-tennessean/177436033/|newspaper=[[The Tennessean]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=April 25, 2024|page=B3|title=Chris Manon commits to transfer to Vanderbilt|author=Gerson, Aria}} {{Open access}} He averaged 9.9 points and 3.7 rebounds per game as a [[sophomore]] in 2021–22 and then averaged 11 points and 3.6 rebounds per game as a [[Junior (education year)|junior]] in 2022–23, also setting Cornell's record for single-season steals (63) in the latter season. In his senior year at Cornell, 2023–24, he was unanimously selected first-team All–[[Ivy League]] after averaging 12.5 points and four rebounds per game while being the conference leader in steals and steal percentage.{{Cite news|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/rookie/2025/07/21/lakers-chris-manon-vanderbilt-two-way-contract/85314241007/|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|title=Report: Vanderbilt forward Chris Mañon to sign two-way contract with Lakers|date=July 21, 2025|author=Taylor, Cody}} Mañon transferred to the [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt Commodores]] for a final season in 2024–25. At Vanderbilt, he averaged 6.6 points and 3.7 rebounds per game. His role was primarily defensive, which he described as "guard the best players on the other team and make life hell for them." ==Professional career== Mañon played with the [[Golden State Warriors]] during the [[2025 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/vanderbilt/basketball/doing-all-the-little-things-chris-manon-is-standing-out-for-golden-state-warriors-without-heavy-scoring-load|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title="Doing all the little things" Chris Mañon is standing out for Golden State Warriors without heavy scoring load|date=July 6, 2025|author=Dwyer, Joey}}{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/vanderbilt/basketball/chris-manon-has-loud-impact-in-first-nba-summer-league-game|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Chris Mañon has loud impact in first NBA Summer League game|date=July 5, 2025|author=Dwyer, Joey}} He was the team's leading scorer with 55 points and was also their leader in rebounds per game (5.2) and blocked shots (8).{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/nba-rumors-chris-manon-lakers-contract/1863109/|publisher=[[NBC Sports Bay Area]]|title=Warriors reportedly lose NBA Summer League standout Chris Mañon to Lakers |date=July 21, 2025|author=Johnson, Dalton}} He scored 17 points in his last game and averaged 11 points with the Warriors. Afterwards, Mañon signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on July 24, 2025.{{Cite news|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2025/07/21/chris-manon-los-angeles-lakers-nba-vanderbilt-basketball/85314898007/|newspaper=[[The Tennessean]]|title=Vanderbilt basketball's Chris Mañon to join Los Angeles Lakers on two-way contact|date=July 21, 2025|author=Morris, Alaina}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-sign-guard-chris-manon-to-two-way-contract|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|date=July 24, 2025|title=Lakers Sign Guard Chris Mañon to Two-Way Contract}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2025}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A.
